findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong substring indices, so it never verifies the grant shortcut
findings.body: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the check `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` is inverted: it fails the match when the grant shortcut *equals* the expected value, and it reads the wrong characters. The encoded token ID is '<2-char sessionType><2-char tokenType><2-char grantType>:<uuid>' (see DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider, which uses substring(4, 6) for the grant shortcut), so the grant shortcut is at indices 4-5, not 3-4. With both bugs combined, for a correctly encoded ID like 'onrtac:<uuid>' the matcher extracts 'ta', which never equals the expected 'ac', so the early-return is skipped and the matcher only checks that the tail is a UUID. Consequently all the updated assertions (expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectAuthReqIdToToken) pass regardless of which grant type was encoded, and a regression that encodes the wrong (or any) grant shortcut would go undetected. The line should be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

findings.title: Shortcut length is not enforced although the encoder/decoder hard-codes exactly 2 characters per grant shortcut
findings.body: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider encodes the token ID as sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantShortcut + ':' + rawId, and getTokenContextFromTokenId rejects any prefix whose length is not exactly 6 (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java line 74). That means every grant shortcut must be exactly 2 characters. However, the getShortcut() contract documented here only says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut', and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit does not validate shortcut length (it only detects duplicate IDs/shortcuts via map sizes). A custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory returning a 1- or 3-character shortcut will still have its tokens issued successfully by encodeTokenId, but those token IDs will then be undecodable: getTokenContextFromTokenId will throw IllegalArgumentException ('Expected length of 6'). The SPI should either document/enforce a 2-character requirement (fail fast in postInit) or the encoder should not assume fixed widths.

findings.title: Breaking SPI changes: public Context copy constructor removed and abstract getShortcut() added to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory
findings.body: This PR removes the public copy constructor `Context(Context context)` from OAuth2GrantType.Context and adds a new abstract method `getShortcut()` to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory. Both are part of the grant-type SPI that third-party extensions implement (custom grant types are an explicitly supported extension point, and the PR description relies on custom grants being addable). Existing custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations will fail to load/compile after upgrade (abstract method not implemented), and any code using the Context copy constructor will break at compile time. At minimum this needs a release-note/api-change mention; preferably getShortcut() should have a default implementation (e.g., deriving from getId()) so existing providers keep working.

findings.title: getTokenContextFromTokenId throws for unknown 6-char prefixes instead of degrading gracefully, unlike the legacy-ID path
findings.body: getTokenContextFromTokenId handles a legacy token ID without ':' by returning an UNKNOWN context (line 68-69), but if the ID contains ':' with a 6-character prefix that does not map to known shortcuts, it throws IllegalArgumentException (lines 74-93). This is reachable with perfectly valid tokens: grant shortcuts come from OAuth2GrantTypeFactory providers, and several of them are EnvironmentDependentProviderFactory implementations (CIBA, device flow, token exchange, pre-authorized code). A token issued while such a feature is enabled will encode e.g. 'ci'; after a restart with the feature disabled, the factory is not returned by getProviderFactoriesStream, so neither the cached map nor the lazy-refresh lookup in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getGrantTypeByShortcut finds it, and decoding a still-valid token ID throws an unchecked exception rather than returning UNKNOWN. Same for shortcuts from uninstalled custom providers. The decode path should fall back to UNKNOWN (like the no-colon case) rather than throwing, or callers must be specified to handle this.

findings.title: Constructor null-check for rawTokenId checks grantType twice
findings.body: Line 73 reads `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` — it duplicates the grantType check from line 72 instead of validating rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is silently accepted (the intended guard never runs), and the error message names the wrong field. The line should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`.

findings.title: Lazy map refresh in getShortcutByGrantType can silently overwrite an existing shortcut mapping, bypassing the duplicate-shortcut validation
findings.body: postInit validates that no two grant factories share an ID or shortcut by comparing map sizes, but the lazy refresh path in getShortcutByGrantType (and getGrantTypeByShortcut) blindly does `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)` for a grant discovered at runtime (e.g., hot-deployed provider). If the newly discovered grant uses a shortcut that already maps to a different grant type, the forward mapping is overwritten while the reverse mapping keeps both entries, so token IDs issued earlier with that shortcut will now decode to the wrong grant type, and the inconsistency is never detected. The refresh path should check for a conflicting existing mapping (and ideally the postInit size check is not a sufficient duplicate detector either — it misses collisions only detectable by checking each key).

findings.title: grantType is captured from formParams at construction and not updated by setFormParams
findings.body: The new grantType field is initialized once in the Context constructor from `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)`. The class still exposes setFormParams(...), which replaces the form parameters, but grantType keeps the value from the original params. Any code path that swaps form params after construction (the mutator exists precisely for that) will then read a stale grant type via getGrantType(); since OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse now copies context.getGrantType() into the client session context, that stale value ends up encoded into the access token ID (e.g., a token-exchange flow reusing a context would record the wrong grant). grantType should be recomputed in setFormParams, or derived lazily in getGrantType().

findings.title: Unit test bypasses factory postInit, so startup validation and real grant registry are untested; no end-to-end test asserts the issued token ID format
findings.body: The test constructs DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, calls init(null), and then overwrites the package-private grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts maps by hand with only two grant types. This means the postInit logic — including the duplicate-shortcut/ID validation that is the main safety net for the encoding scheme — is never exercised, nor is the lazy-refresh path against a real KeycloakSessionFactory (sessionFactory is null in the test, so those branches would NPE if hit). Additionally there is no integration test asserting that a real token endpoint response produces an ID like 'onrtac:<uuid>' for the authorization-code grant; the only place that could catch this (AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId) is itself broken (see separate finding), so the actual wire format is effectively unverified.
